title: Choose Paperlight's visual world
question: The roll dealt Swiss Grid. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Swiss Grid
options.lineage: International Typographic Style posters, Zürich and Basel, 1950s–60s
options.thesis: Every document sits on a visible modular grid; structure is carried by scale and flat colour fields.
options.viewport: A vermilion Prose rail at left, the page on a white grid, and the outline as an index of oversized section numerals.
options.risk: Can feel cold and austere if the colour fields are set timidly.

raised.raise: Document state is stamped, never hidden: Saved, Unsaved and Exported marks with their times.
Panels divide by hairlines, not shadows, and Delete or Discard always sits apart with deliberate space.
Focus mode lifts the paragraph you are writing and dims the rest of the page.
Each outline numeral carries a bar whose length is that section's word count.
The style picker previews every paragraph style at its true size.

options.label: Paperback Bands
options.thesis: Each app is a colour-coded series, and every screen keeps the paperback's three horizontal bands.
options.viewport: An orange top band names Prose and the document, a white middle band holds the page, and an orange foot band carries status.
options.risk: The most familiar idea on this table; it can read as a retro book-cover costume.

options.label: Transit Map
options.lineage: Metropolitan rail diagrams in vitreous enamel
options.thesis: The suite as a transit network: each app is a coloured line, and every document is a station on it.
options.viewport: A midnight-blue shell, a white page, and the outline drawn as a scarlet line with headings as stations and a you-are-here ring.
options.case: Four coloured lines map cleanly onto four apps and read instantly on camera; it loses on clarity inside dense editors.
options.risk: A dark navy shell all day can feel heavy for daylight writing.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: Time reads upward and every block's length is its exact duration.
options.viewport: A vertical centre staff with documents as shaped blocks.
options.case: Fuses poorly: viewers can't read the notation, and documents aren't timelines.
options.kept: Length that means something: outline bars sized by section length.
options.risk: Opaque to anyone who can't read a score.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: One journey as tear-off coupons, each state stamped on the paper.
options.viewport: Documents as coupons in a paper wallet.
options.case: Fuses poorly: coupons fit itineraries, not documents.
options.risk: A novelty that tires in daily use.

options.label: Title Card Wall
options.thesis: Rows of artwork where the focused tile grows and the rest dims.
options.viewport: Recent files as rows of poster tiles.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it suits browsing, not writing.
options.kept: Focus lifts and the rest dims, as a writing focus mode.
options.risk: Turns a work tool into a catalogue.

options.label: Developer Console
options.thesis: Graphite panels split by one-pixel seams.
options.viewport: Persistent tiled panels around the page.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a developer-tool costume for writers and students.
options.kept: Hairline seams and isolated destructive actions.
options.risk: Alienates anyone who isn't a developer.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms carry everything; scale contrast is the only hierarchy.
options.viewport: A giant glyph with live sliders.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a font showroom, not an office suite.
options.kept: Paragraph styles preview at their true size.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern office suite, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: A slim top toolbar, a white page centred on light grey, and a file panel on the left.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the familiar suites by design.
